candidate.document:
Nishimura typed the request at two in the morning, the Kitakyushu card three days out: *Write Kuroneko vs. Takeda, Pacific Junior title. Takeda retains by cheating.*

Musonius sent back questions before a single line of match. Did Takeda's character cheat sloppily or cleverly? Was the referee already established as easy to distract? Did Kuroneko's mask have a storyline weight, or was it only costume?

"Sloppy," Nishimura answered. "Ref is Ogata, he's slow. Mask matters. His late father wore it."

So Musonius built the draft around the mask. Kuroneko flies early: topes to the floor, a springboard that the Hakata crowd will be waiting for. Takeda grinds him down on the apron. Near the twelfth minute Kuroneko hits his finisher clean, and Ogata counts two before Takeda's second drags the referee out by the ankle. In the confusion Takeda yanks the mask half off. Kuroneko covers his face with both hands, and Takeda rolls him up with a fistful of tights. Three.

Under the draft Musonius added a note. *The pin comes while he's protecting the mask, so the crowd sees he chose his father's mask over the belt. That gives him a reason for the rematch nobody has to explain. Do you want Ogata to see the tights on the replay screen afterward, or keep him blind until the next show?*

Nishimura read it twice. "Blind. I want people angry on the train home."

"Then cut the replay," Musonius wrote, and did. "One more question. Does Kuroneko get the mask back in the ring, or does Takeda leave with it?"

"Leave with it."

"That's a much heavier story to carry into next month. It works if you're sure you'll run the rematch. Are you?"

Nishimura looked at the October calendar, which was still mostly blank.

"Let me ask Yamauchi-san," he typed, and left the line open.
